Trace of a bump to 3.15: ci.yml matrix is [3.11,3.12,3.13,3.14] and the audit matrix is [3.11,3.12,3.14], so the assert fails. A bump to 3.13 passes the unit matrix but fails the audit matrix, so a version present in only one matrix is also caught. A bump that changes the tag format makes the unpack or regex fail instead (and test 1 fails), so it is not silently accepted. docker/Dockerfile has both stages FROM the same python base (lines 6, 31). The only apt installs are build-essential/libpq-dev in the builder, which is discarded, and libpq5/ca-certificates/tini in the runtime (lines 16-18, 45-48). None install another Python, and the runtime copies only /root/.local from the builder. The comment's claim is accurate for what the test asserts.

tests/unit/test_docker_inputs.py:23-30 extracts the single Python version from the Dockerfile FROM lines, then for ci.yml job 'unit' and dependency-audit.yml job 'audit' asserts it is in strategy.matrix.python-version. Both jobs exist (ci.yml:32, dependency-audit.yml:14) with matrices ['3.11','3.12','3.13','3.14'] and ['3.11','3.12','3.14']; Dockerfile uses 3.14. Counter-inputs: a bump to 3.15 absent from either matrix gives AssertionError; a missing job or matrix key gives KeyError; an unquoted YAML float (3.14) is not equal to the string '3.14', so the assert fails; a non-3.x tag, or two different versions across stages, breaks the single-element unpack and raises. Every such case fails the test, so the doc claim holds.
